arguments.text:
Fixed. Root cause: `Interval.fromISO` (src/interval.js) parsed *both* halves of the string with `DateTime.fromISO` before falling back to `Duration.fromISO` for the `<date>/<duration>` and `<duration>/<date>` forms. With `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true`, `DateTime.invalid(...)` throws immediately, so the duration half blew up with `InvalidDateTimeError` before the duration fallback could ever run.

The two `DateTime.fromISO` probes are now wrapped in try/catch and their validity is recorded in `startIsValid` / `endIsValid`, so a half that is a duration (not a date) simply counts as "not a date" and the existing `Duration.fromISO` fallback handles it. Genuinely unparsable input still produces an invalid Interval (and still throws `InvalidIntervalError` when `throwOnInvalid` is set).

Verified:
- `Interval.fromISO("2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M")` and `"PT5H30M/2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00"` now return the same valid intervals with `throwOnInvalid` on as with it off.
- `<date>/<date>` still works; `"foo/bar"` still throws `InvalidIntervalError`; `"2020-06-23/2020-06-22"` still throws for end-before-start.
- Full jest suite: 892 passing, only the 2 pre-existing locale-dependent `toFormat('FFFF')` French-locale failures remain (they failed before my change too). `eslint` clean.

Status:
- #4 (Duration.normalize → NaN): FIXED. The unit-conversion matrix was missing two factors: `years.quarters` (4) and `quarters.seconds` in the casual matrix (and `years.quarters` in the longterm/accurate matrix). Dividing by an undefined factor produced NaN. Restored the missing entries; a sweep over every unit pair × both conversion accuracies now produces zero NaNs, and your two examples return `{years:1, quarters:2}` and `{quarters:1, seconds:2}`.
- #5 (negative-year ISO output): FIXED. `padStart` in src/impl/util.js counted the "-" as a digit, so `-1` padded to width 4 became `00-1`. It now pads the magnitude and re-attaches the sign: `-0001-01-01`, `-0010-01-01`, and positive years are unchanged.
- #3 (isInDST for 1974): still working, ETA ~12 min. Root cause is the `isInDST` heuristic (it compares against January/May of the same year, which breaks when a zone's DST schedule is unusual, as in 1974 when US DST ran Jan 6 – Oct 27). I'm making it agree with the zone's real DST status for every instant of 1974 while keeping normal years correct.
Full jest suite still shows only the 2 pre-existing locale-dependent toFormat('FFF'/'FFFF') failures.

arguments.text:
#6 (FixedOffsetZone accepting a non-numeric offset): FIXED. `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` was hard-coded to `true`; it now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`. So `new FixedOffsetZone("CDT").isValid` is `false`, and `DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone })` is invalid with `invalidReason === "unsupported zone"` (the DateTime constructor already rejects invalid zones). Numeric fixed offsets are unaffected.

#3 (isInDST for 1974): FIXED. `isInDST` used to compare the current offset against the offsets of January 1 and May 1 of the same year, which assumes January is standard time and May is DST. In 1974 US DST ran Jan 6 – Oct 27, so that heuristic was wrong for almost the whole year (it reported false for the entire DST period except the first 5 days of each month). It now derives the standard offset from the year's January/May offsets (works in both hemispheres) and checks the local day as well as the instant, so it agrees with the zone's real DST status for every hour of 1973–1975 in America/Los_Angeles, and normal years, southern-hemisphere zones, UTC and invalid DateTimes all behave as before. Your repro now returns true.
Full suite: 892 passing, only the 2 pre-existing locale-dependent toFormat('FFF'/'FFFF') failures. eslint clean.

#6 fixed and verified (see my reply on #3 for details): `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`, so a non-numeric offset yields an invalid zone and any DateTime built from it is invalid with `invalidReason === "unsupported zone"`. Full jest suite: 892 passing, only the 2 pre-existing locale-dependent toFormat failures; eslint clean.
